title: Trial begins in case of man accused of Bogie triple murder

By Chloe Chomicki

Topic:Courts

Darryl Valroy Young, 63, has pleaded not guilty to three counts of murder and one count of attempted murder. (ABC News: Carole Howlett)

The trial of a man accused of murdering three people and attempting to murder another person on a remote Queensland cattle property in 2022 has begun in Townsville.

Darryl Valroy Young, 63, pleaded not guilty to three counts of murder and one count of attempted murder in the Supreme Court on Monday morning.

The court heard the trial, expected to run for three weeks, will hear from dozens of witnesses including Ross Tighe who Mr Young is accused of attempting to murder.

A man accused of murdering three people and attempting to murder another person on a rural Queensland property has pleaded not guilty at the opening of a three-week Supreme Court trial in Townsville.

Darryl Valroy Young, 63, is charged with three counts of murder and one count of attempted murder.

Police say Maree and Mervyn Schwarz were killed in a shooting incident in the rural north Queensland community of Bogie on August 4, 2022.  (Supplied)

The court heard Mr Young is accused of murdering Mervyn Schwarz, Maree Schwarz and Graham Tighe by using a firearm to shoot each of them in the head at a property in Bogie, north-west of Mackay, on August 4, 2022.

Mr Young is also accused of attempting to murder Ross Tighe during the same incident.

Police say Graham Tighe was also shot dead during the incident on a Bogie cattle property on August 4, 2022. (Facebook)

Mr Young appeared in the courtroom wearing a long-sleeve navy button down shirt and black pants.

He listened to proceedings in the courtroom through earphones that were connected to a listening device.

A jury of 12 people, six men and six women, and an additional three men empanelled as reserve jurors, heard opening statements by the crown.

Mr Young's lawyer told jurors he denied ever seeing the Schwarzs or the Tighes on the day they were shot.  (ABC News: Carole Howlett)

Prosecutor David Nardone told jurors that Ross Tighe would give evidence in the trial and explain that on August 4, 2022, he, his mother, his brother and his stepfather were shot at the gate of Mr Young's Shannonvale Station.

"The man that Ross Tighe saw wielding the rifle is the accused Darryl Valroy Young," Mr Nardone.

"The most important witness you will hear from in this trial is Ross Tighe, it is the evidence of Ross Tighe that you will receive first when that begins tomorrow."

Prosecutor David Nardone (right) is appearing on behalf of the crown.  (ABC News: Chloe Chomicki)

Mr Nardone said Mr and Mrs Schwarz and Ross Tighe had been visiting Graham Tighe who lived at Sutherland Station in August 2022 to assist with mustering cattle.

He said Graham Tighe received a call from his neighbour, Mr Young, on August 3, 2022.

"Darryl Young angrily accused Graham Tighe of selling calves that belonged to him," he said.

He said two people at Graham Tighe's home overheard the phone call in which Mr Young asked the family to attend the front gate of his property at 8am the following morning.

He said once the family arrived Mr Young began to level accusations once again before arming himself with a rifle.

"The accused Darryl Young walked back to his ute and said something like, 'I'll end this once and for all'," Mr Nardone said.

The Supreme Court trial, being held in Townsville, is expected to run for three weeks. (ABC North Queensland: Tom Major)

The crown prosecutor detailed gunshot wounds suffered by Mr and Mrs Schwarz and the Tighe brothers.

He also described a desperate struggle by Ross Tighe to seek help while critically injured.

Mr Nardone told jurors that both Ross Tighe's evidence and ballistic testing from police would support the crown case that Mr Young used a rifle, which he was not licensed to carry, to shoot Mr and Mrs Schwarz and the Tighe brothers.

He also said that jurors would be shown photos from trail cameras at the gate of Mr Young's property which Ross Tighe said were missing on August 4, 2022.

"You will be asked to infer that the trail cameras usually at that gate were taken down hours before the killing," Mr Nardone.

Defence lawyer Anthony J Kimmins (right) is representing Mr Young.  (ABC News: Chloe Chomicki)

Defence lawyer Anthony J Kimmins told jurors that Mr Young denied ever having a phone call about missing cattle with Graham Tighe on August 3, 2022 or meeting with the family at the gate of Shannonvale Station on the following morning.

"He is accused of slaughtering three members of one family and attempting to slaughter a fourth," Mr Kimmins said.

"He has been given nicknames; the beast of Bogie, the butcher of Bogie.

Mr Young silently watched on as the crown and his defence lawyer gave opening statements on Monday. ( ABC News: Carole Howlett)

"The fact that he is accused of committing these offences does not prove anything, nor do the nicknames.

"Darryl Young is presumed to be innocent of each and every one of these offences."

Mr Kimmins said Mr Young and his neighbours worked collaboratively and had reinstated 8 kilometres of fence line between the properties weeks before the alleged shooting.

He asked jurors to consider the working relationship between the two families and whether missing cattle was a plausible motive for the "slaughter or attempted slaughter of a family".

Mr Kimmins said throughout the trial the defence would challenge other aspects of the case including whether other persons had a motive to kill.

He said the defence would also question how Ross Tighe suffered a gunshot to the abdomen when he was supposedly running away from gunfire.

The trial continues.
